title.title: Same embedded topology, different multiplicity
title.subtitle: Claim: hypersurface germs that are ambiently homeomorphic with multiplicities 2 and 3, and 4 and 5

plain: Two equations whose solution sets have the same shape, even inside space, yet different lowest degrees

object.axisLabel: multiplicity: lowest degree of the equation

beats.text: Zariski asked: does the embedded topology of a singularity fix its multiplicity?
Claimed: two pairs of germs with the same topology and different multiplicities
The method: different lowest degrees, congruent Seifert forms

steps: In high dimensions, one algebraic table decides the topology
Build two equations whose tables match
But their lowest degrees differ: two versus three

achievement.label: Zariski's multiplicity question (1971)
achievement.context: Before: true for plane curves and for multiplicity 1 (A'Campo, Lê), widely believed true

verify.detail: No Lean; the topology rests on a surgery-theoretic classification
verify.ourCheck: We read the claim and caveats; we did not check the proof

voice.text: Zariski asked whether the embedded topology of a singularity determines its multiplicity.
In high dimensions, the Seifert form decides topology; match it, change the degree.
Claimed: no, with multiplicities two and three.

sources.quote: Zariski asked in 1971 whether the embedded topology of a hypersurface singularity determines its multiplicity.
It is true for plane curves and for multiplicity 1 (A'Campo, Lê)
